text:
alex: Quick idea — we should add a "handback" flow for cross-project service keys so ownership can be returned to org-level when a project is archived. currently keys stay bound to a dead project and quota attribution gets messy.
mira: yup, seen that with billing spikes when projects are recreated. How would handback affect routing / quota attribution?
sam: two options: 1) remap existing key -> org-backed ephemeral project for quota & metrics, 2) reissue a org-scoped key and mark old key as redirected. option 1 preserves existing key id but complicates authz.
alex: i prefer option 2 (reissue) for clarity: revoke old token, mint org token, write redirect entry in auth proxy that accepts both for 24h. fewer surprises for billing.
lisa: UX question — how do we present this in console? admin clicks "handback" on project page, shows dependent services list + a single checkbox to reissue keys. maybe show cost/credit impact.
mira: +1. Also need telemetry: signal which calls switched, latency of fallback, and quota attribution by origin before/after. we should add an event type `auth.key.handback` to ingest pipeline.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout plan for auth-proxy v2 will start at 1726349000 to 1726352600 in us-west1 with flag `auth.handback.enabled=true`.
sam: implementation note: auth-proxy should accept header `X-Original-Project` and map to org token when redirect table exists. example: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer OLD_KEY
X-Original-Project: project-xyz
```
proxy rewrites internal principal to org:org-123 and logs `handback=true`.
devex: testing — we need a small integration script to simulate reissues and ensure client libs surface the new key and don't break retries. i can add a quick snippet in the node SDK tests.
lisa: console UI should show a 24h rollback button after handback in case customers want to revert. also record acceptance checkbox for compliance.
mira: telemetry queries: we want counts of `auth.key.handback` events, redirect hit rate, and number of distinct callers that saw the fallback. can we emit dimensions: old_key_id, new_key_id, project_before, org_after, reason?
alex: keep PII out — avoid logging full caller ids, just hashed client_id. add a sampling bucket for edge cases.
sam: quota behavior: when old key is revoked and org-key comes in, we should maintain continuity of per-customer rate limits. propose an attribution window: 48h where usage is counted towards the original project for billing reconciliation, but enforcement uses org quota to keep apps running.
mira: sounds good. ops: add alerts if redirect error rate > 0.5% in canary.
infra-bot: observability: metric `auth.handback.redirect_errors` and `auth.handback.redirect_success` created. dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/example/d/handback
devex: rollout steps suggestion: feature flag + internal canary (10% orgs) -> monitor 48h -> expand to 50% -> full. include migration-runbook in the console and a dry-run mode that simulates reissue without changing keys.
lisa: one more UI thing: show which dependent services had their keys reissued with a copy/paste box and TTL recommendations.
alex: i'll draft the RFC and include an appendix with sample BigQuery telemetry queries and the minimal auth-proxy change. can someone volunteer to own the canary monitoring?
mira: i'll own monitoring for the canary window.
sam: i'll handle the proxy changes and tests. devex will help with SDK bumps.
devex: yep, will add test coverage and a short migration guide.
alex: great — moving to action items: alex -> write RFC by EOD tomorrow, sam -> prototype redirect table this week, mira -> create Grafana panels and alerts, lisa -> mock console flow. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
